about: The weekly briefing's thresholds. scripts/briefing_numbers.py reads this file, and so do apps that compute the same numbers, so change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.min_visits: Categories, products and brands with fewer visits than this in both periods are left out.
notes.min_sessions: Searches with fewer sessions than this in both periods are left out.
notes.movers_top: Rows in each rising and falling movers list.
notes.list_top: Rows in the top searches and top categories lists.
notes.issue_top: Rows in the searches and categories with issues lists.
notes.peers: A row is judged against the median of this many highest-traffic rows.
notes.low_conversion_ratio: Conversion below this share of the typical conversion is an issue.
notes.high_bounce_ratio: Bounce above this multiple of the typical bounce is an issue, when it is also high_bounce_min_points or more above it.
notes.revenue_drop_ratio: Revenue below this share of last period's is an issue, when the drop is also revenue_drop_min or more.
notes.revenue_drop_min: See revenue_drop_ratio, in the account's currency.
notes.dead_end_bounce_pct: A row with no product views and at least this bounce rate is a dead end.
